summary: @onereach/ui-components-common preinstall downloads Bun runtime and executes an obfuscated 727KB blob
details: The published tarball ships two files at the tarball root that are not declared in package.json `files` (which lists only `dist`, `src`, `./shims.d.ts`, `./tsconfig.components.json`): `setup.mjs` and a 727KB single-line obfuscated JavaScript file `math_init.js`. package.json declares `scripts.preinstall: "node setup.mjs"`, causing setup.mjs to run automatically on `npm install`. setup.mjs downloads the Bun runtime from `https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v<version>/...` into a temporary directory, extracts it, chmods it executable, and then `execFileSync`s the Bun binary against the sibling `math_init.js`. math_init.js is a `// @bun @bun-cjs` Bun-compiled bundle with a rotating string-array decoder (`WV8StW`), hex-mangled identifiers, and a large numeric constants table used to reconstruct strings at runtime; no plaintext URLs or readable behavior remain. The package advertises itself as a Vue UI-components library, which has no legitimate need to fetch an alternate JavaScript runtime and execute an opaque payload under it at install time. Running the payload under a freshly-downloaded Bun interpreter bypasses Node-based inspection tooling that only traces Node-reachable code. The combination of an undeclared tarball blob, alternate-runtime dropper in preinstall, and 727KB of obfuscated Bun-compiled code is consistent with a compromised release rather than legitimate maintainer behavior.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
